scope_note: AI export: display coordinates are arbitrary schematic units. Values and provenance labels are copied from code, not independently certified apparatus facts. Null defaults include NaN in source.

bpd_bandwidth_hz.note: PDB450A RF bandwidth at the 1e5 V/A gain setting (150/45/4/0.3/0.1 MHz for 1e3..1e7 V/A).

bpd_cw_saturation_w.note: PDB450A CW saturation power at 820 nm. Optical damage threshold is 20 mW.

bpd_nep_w_per_rthz.note: PDB450A minimum NEP, DC to 4 MHz, gain 1e5 V/A. WARNING: specified with the STOCK photodiode. This unit has S3883 diodes fitted, which changes junction capacitance and therefore the amplifier noise gain. Replace with a measured dark trace before trusting any clearance number.

bpd_transimpedance_v_per_a.note: Transimpedance gain stated in Sim et al.

etalon_fsr_hz.note: Free spectral range. Deliberately incommensurate with 3.036 GHz, so no unwanted sideband lands on a transmission peak.

etalon_fwhm_hz.note: Passband FWHM; with the FSR this gives finesse 17.9.

etalon_leak.note: Stopband floor per stage, solved from the paper's two-etalon carrier:seed ratio of ~0.5 percent. An ideal Airy cascade predicts far deeper suppression, so without this floor the model overestimates seed purity and therefore squeezing. It lumps surface scatter, the finite angular spread of a real beam washing out the resonance, alignment, and the measurement floor. It is fitted to ONE published number, not measured: a real transmission scan should replace it.

etalon_peak_transmission.note: Per-stage peak transmission including realistic alignment. The paper quotes 85 percent as the etalon specification.

etalon_stages.note: Three sequential etalons. The paper reports ~0.5 percent carrier:seed with two and much less with three.

eom_insertion_loss_db.note: Fiber-EOM insertion loss including connectors. Back-solved so that J1(beta)^2 times this loss reproduces the reported ~10 percent minus-first-order efficiency; it is not a separately measured figure.

eom_max_input_w.note: Optical power above which the fiber EOM stops modulating properly. This is the binding constraint on the whole seed path.

eom_orthogonal_leakage.note: Fraction of polarization-mismatched light that leaves the modulator as unmodulated carrier. Zero for a single-polarization LiNbO3 waveguide: the mismatched component becomes coupling loss instead of carrier contamination.

eom_v_pi_v.note: RF half-wave voltage at ~3 GHz for an EOSPACE AZ-0S5-10 class modulator. Placeholder: measure the sideband ratio versus RF power to fix it. At 18 dBm this gives beta = 1.79, close to the J1 maximum at 1.841, which is consistent with 18 dBm having been chosen to maximise the seed.

loss_ecdl_to_ta.note: Isolator and steering optics between the ECDL and the amplifier. Placeholder.

pbs_extinction_ratio.note: Extinction of the PBS used for polarization rejection of the pump after the cell.

pd_active_diameter_mm.note: Hamamatsu S3883 photosensitive diameter, 1.7 mm^2. The stock PDB450A diode is 0.8 mm.

pd_max_power_density_w_per_cm2.note: Thorlabs linearity limit for the PDB450A. The manual also asks that the beam illuminate the whole active area, so a hard focus onto the diode is doubly discouraged.

pd_responsivity_a_per_w.note: Hamamatsu S3883 photosensitivity at 795 nm, read off the spectral-response curve. Implies QE = 1240*0.58/795 = 90.45 percent, matching the 90.47 percent quoted in the paper. The stock PDB450A Si diode peaks at 0.53 A/W, i.e. QE <= 82.7 percent.

post_cell_loss_pct.note: Optical loss between the cell and the detector, the `loss_pct` knob in the GABES FWM scheme.

pump_collimator_diameter_mm.note: Collimated 1/e^2 diameter out of the pump fiber collimator, from the setup drawing.

pump_fiber_efficiency.note: Free space to fiber coupling on the pump path. Placeholder; this one directly sets the available pump power.

pump_seed_angle_deg.note: Crossing angle in the cell. Stated as an empirical choice, so it is a candidate for optimisation rather than a fixed constant.

pump_telescope_f1_mm.note: First lens of the pump telescope (from the setup drawing).

pump_telescope_f2_mm.note: Second lens of the pump telescope; magnification 150/300 = 0.5.

seed_collimator_diameter_mm.note: Collimated 1/e^2 diameter out of the seed fiber collimator, from the setup drawing.

seed_fiber_in_efficiency.note: Coupling into the fiber EOM. Placeholder. Not power-critical: the seed path has large headroom and is deliberately attenuated afterwards.

seed_fiber_out_efficiency.note: Coupling out of the seed chain into the delivery fiber.

seed_telescope_f1_mm.note: First lens of the seed telescope (from the setup drawing).

seed_telescope_f2_mm.note: Second lens of the seed telescope; magnification 150/400 = 0.375.

ta_ase_fraction.note: Broadband amplified spontaneous emission as a fraction of amplifier output. Placeholder. Removed from coherent power rather than tracked as a spectral line: it is not at any FWM-relevant frequency and the etalons erase it in the seed path.

ta_m2_out.note: Beam-quality factor out of the tapered amplifier. Placeholder, but it matters: it is what makes fiber coupling after the amplifier lossy.

ta_saturation_w.note: Seed power at which the amplifier reaches half its maximum output. Placeholder; fix it together with the slope from one P-I curve at known seed power.

ta_slope_w_per_a.note: Slope of the amplifier's maximum output versus drive current. Placeholder chosen so the nominal operating point gives about 1.4 W.

waist_scale_factor.note: Collimator diameter times telescope magnification underestimates the paper's cell waists by a consistent 6-10 percent (500 vs 530 um pump, 300 vs 330 um seed). One shared factor absorbs it. The consistency across two independent paths suggests a definition difference (1/e^2 versus 4-sigma or FWHM in the quoted collimator diameters) rather than two coincidences.

t_m_mopa_out.note: Per-pass transmission of m_mopa_out. Steering mirror, protected-silver order of magnitude.

t_oi_mopa.note: Per-pass transmission of OI. Optical isolator. The lossiest passive element on the table.

t_hwp_split.note: Per-pass transmission of HWP. Waveplate, AR-coated both faces.

t_m_split_1.note: Per-pass transmission of m_split_1. Steering mirror, protected-silver order of magnitude.

t_m_split_2.note: Per-pass transmission of m_split_2. Steering mirror, protected-silver order of magnitude.

t_pbs_split.note: Per-pass transmission of PBS. Polarizing cube, insertion loss on the used port.

t_f230_pump.note: Per-pass transmission of F230. Set to 1 deliberately: this element's throughput is already carried by `pump_fiber_efficiency`, and counting it twice would quietly halve the budget.

t_pol_seed.note: Per-pass transmission of Polarizer. Sheet/Glan polarizer.

t_noise_eater.note: Per-pass transmission of Noise eater. Intensity-noise servo; only its throughput is modelled.

t_m_seed_1.note: Per-pass transmission of m_seed_1. Steering mirror, protected-silver order of magnitude.

t_hwp_eom.note: Per-pass transmission of HWP. Waveplate, AR-coated both faces.

t_f220_eom_in.note: Per-pass transmission of F220. Set to 1 deliberately: this element's throughput is already carried by `seed_fiber_in_efficiency`, and counting it twice would quietly halve the budget.

t_eom.note: Per-pass transmission of fiber EOM. Set to 1 deliberately: this element's throughput is already carried by `eom_insertion_loss_db`, and counting it twice would quietly halve the budget.

t_f220_eom_out.note: Per-pass transmission of F220. Set to 1 deliberately: this element's throughput is already carried by `seed_fiber_out_efficiency`, and counting it twice would quietly halve the budget.

t_etalon_1.note: Per-pass transmission of Etalon 1. Set to 1 deliberately: this element's throughput is already carried by `etalon_peak_transmission`, and counting it twice would quietly halve the budget.

t_m_et_1.note: Per-pass transmission of m_et_1. Steering mirror, protected-silver order of magnitude.

t_hwp_etalon.note: Per-pass transmission of HWP. Waveplate, AR-coated both faces.

t_m_et_2.note: Per-pass transmission of m_et_2. Steering mirror, protected-silver order of magnitude.

t_etalon_2.note: Per-pass transmission of Etalon 2. Set to 1 deliberately: this element's throughput is already carried by `etalon_peak_transmission`, and counting it twice would quietly halve the budget.

t_etalon_3.note: Per-pass transmission of Etalon 3. Set to 1 deliberately: this element's throughput is already carried by `etalon_peak_transmission`, and counting it twice would quietly halve the budget.

t_gt_seed.note: Per-pass transmission of GT. Glan-Taylor: calcite plus two surfaces.

t_m_seed_out.note: Per-pass transmission of m_seed_out. Steering mirror, protected-silver order of magnitude.

t_m_seed_down.note: Per-pass transmission of m_seed_down. Steering mirror, protected-silver order of magnitude.

t_f220_seed.note: Per-pass transmission of F220. Set to 1 deliberately: this element's throughput is already carried by `seed_fiber_out_efficiency`, and counting it twice would quietly halve the budget.

t_col_seed.note: Per-pass transmission of 5724 · 1.6 mm. Set to 1 deliberately: this element's throughput is already carried by `seed_fiber_out_efficiency`, and counting it twice would quietly halve the budget.

t_qwp_seed.note: Per-pass transmission of QWP. Waveplate, AR-coated both faces.

t_hwp_seed.note: Per-pass transmission of HWP. Waveplate, AR-coated both faces.

t_seed_l1.note: Per-pass transmission of f=400. Telescope lens, AR-coated.

t_seed_l2.note: Per-pass transmission of f=150. Telescope lens, AR-coated.

t_m_seed_a.note: Per-pass transmission of m_seed_a. Steering mirror, protected-silver order of magnitude.

t_gtp_seed.note: Per-pass transmission of GTP. Glan-Taylor: calcite plus two surfaces.

t_col_pump.note: Per-pass transmission of 5725 · 2.0 mm. Set to 1 deliberately: this element's throughput is already carried by `pump_fiber_efficiency`, and counting it twice would quietly halve the budget.

t_qwp_pump.note: Per-pass transmission of QWP. Waveplate, AR-coated both faces.

t_hwp_pump.note: Per-pass transmission of HWP. Waveplate, AR-coated both faces.

t_pump_l1.note: Per-pass transmission of f=300. Telescope lens, AR-coated.

t_pump_l2.note: Per-pass transmission of f=150. Telescope lens, AR-coated.

t_m_pump_a.note: Per-pass transmission of m_pump_a. Steering mirror, protected-silver order of magnitude.

t_gtp_pump.note: Per-pass transmission of GTP. Glan-Taylor: calcite plus two surfaces.

t_pbs_in.note: Per-pass transmission of PBS. Polarizing cube, insertion loss on the used port.

t_cell.note: Per-pass transmission of Rb cell. Both vapour-cell windows, uncoated-glass order of magnitude.

t_pbs_out.note: Per-pass transmission of PBS. Polarizing cube, insertion loss on the used port.

t_dm_probe.note: Per-pass transmission of D-mirror. D-shaped pick-off mirror.

t_dm_conj.note: Per-pass transmission of D-mirror. D-shaped pick-off mirror.

t_iris_probe.note: Per-pass transmission of Iris. Iris, opened past the beam. Pump rejection is no longer modelled here -- see pump_leakage_dbm on the detector.

t_iris_conj.note: Per-pass transmission of Iris. Iris, opened past the beam. Pump rejection is no longer modelled here -- see pump_leakage_dbm on the detector.

t_lens_probe.note: Per-pass transmission of f=75. Singlet, AR-coated.

t_lens_conj.note: Per-pass transmission of f=100. Singlet, AR-coated.

t_bpd.note: Per-pass transmission of Balanced detector. Detector face; its quantum efficiency is the separate pd_responsivity_a_per_w.

loss_post_cell_residual.note: Residual factor on the post-cell transmission, on top of the per-optic values. Solved so the wide-open limit reproduces the 5.5 percent post-cell loss quoted in Sim et al.: the per-optic numbers are nominal guesses while the total is the one measured quantity, so the discrepancy lives here rather than being spread silently over optics nobody measured.

layouts.title: Part 1 — source, amplifier, seed modulation and filtering

nodes.label: 795 nm ECDL
nodes.note: Detuning is set by locking to the reference arm, not by predicting frequency from temperature / current / PZT.

nodes.label: OI
nodes.note: Optical isolator. Loss only; not modelled.

nodes.label: Rb natural
nodes.note: Saturated-absorption reference. The oscilloscope demo lives here: this trace is what the detuning is actually set by.

nodes.label: CL
nodes.note: Cylindrical lens shaping the amplifier input. It is what sets the amplifier's output beam quality, i.e. ta_m2_out.

nodes.label: HWP
nodes.note: The pump-power knob: it sets how the amplifier output divides.

nodes.label: PBS
nodes.note: Pump transmits, seed reflects.

nodes.label: F230
nodes.note: Pump delivery collimator; continues in part 2.

nodes.label: Polarizer
nodes.note: Holds the fiber EOM under its ~10 mW rating. The split alone cannot satisfy both that and the pump power.

nodes.label: Noise eater
nodes.note: Intensity-noise servo. Not modelled, but it acts on exactly the noise a squeezing measurement cares about.

nodes.label: fiber EOM
nodes.note: EOSPACE LiNbO3 phase modulator. The RF offset from the ground-state splitting sets the two-photon detuning. Unwanted-mode RIN is a detector-level input.

nodes.label: HWP
nodes.note: Between etalon 1 and etalon 2 in the drawing.

nodes.label: GT
nodes.note: Glan-Taylor after the filter chain. Part 2 has further GTPs on each arm; the model previously had only one.

nodes.label: F220
nodes.note: Seed delivery collimator; continues in part 2.

nodes.label: PBS

nodes.label: Rb cell
